data.text:
Ginagawa na namang bobo ang mga tao. 

First off, if we really wanted to protect local industries, kung 'yun talaga ang totoong dahilan, eh 'di sana tayo ang nag-impose ng tariffs noon pa! Hahahah.

Because what is a tariff? It’s a protective wall.
And only the importing country builds that wall.

So if the Palace truly wanted to “shield” domestic sectors, then it’s our government that should have been raising or maintaining tariffs on U.S. imports (rice, corn, sugar, poultry) to prevent American goods from flooding our markets 

It’s absurd. The logic collapses on contact with itself.

If the U.S. is the one granting tariff reductions, then the tariff is the U.S.’ tax on Philippine exports.

So when we “opt out,” what happens?

→ The U.S. keeps taxing our exports at 19%.
→ We get no market access.
→ Our exporters, not our farmers, are the ones penalized.

So, by their own admission, they “protected” local producers by allowing the U.S. to tax them higher.

That’s like saying: “To help our farmers, we made sure their products stay more expensive abroad.”

The Palace says we didn’t want to “fully open” our markets to U.S. goods. But we already did.

The Philippines is a WTO member with existing low-tariff ceilings and already imports massive volumes of U.S. wheat, poultry, and dairy under long-standing liberalization programs.

So if “protection” was truly the goal, we could have simply used safeguards or quotas, not rejected tariff cuts that only affected U.S. import taxes, not ours.

Jusko, bobo lang bibili nitong excuse na ibinebenta ng gobyerno.
